value:

Read the following extract about Silas:

‘In old days there were angels who came and took men by the hand and led them away from the city of destruction. We see no white-winged angels now. But yet men are led away from threatening destruction: a hand is put into theirs, which leads them forth gently towards a calm and bright land, so that they look no more backward; and the hand may be a little child’s.’

expect:
Top band (16-20): Perceptive analysis. ‘In old days’ vs ‘now’ creates a shift from divine to human. ‘White-winged angels’ evokes traditional religious imagery, then dismisses it. ‘Hands of little children’ replaces angelic intervention with domestic love. ‘Quiet neighbourhood’ makes community, not heaven, the destination. The extended metaphor redefines redemption: it comes through ordinary people, not supernatural forces. Links to Eppie as Silas’s ‘angel.’
Upper-mid band (11-15): Clear analysis of the religious imagery shift.
Lower-mid band (6-10): Some valid observations.
Lower band (1-5): Simple comments.
value:
Top band (16-20): Perceptive analysis. ‘In old days’ against ‘now’ creates a shift from divine to human. ‘White-winged angels’ evokes traditional religious imagery, then dismisses it. ‘A hand is put into theirs’ keeps the gesture of the angels but strips away the wings. ‘Calm and bright land’ makes an earthly home, not heaven, the destination. The delayed last clause — ‘and the hand may be a little child’s’ — redefines redemption: it comes through ordinary people, not supernatural forces. Links to Eppie as Silas’s ‘angel.’
Upper-mid band (11-15): Clear analysis of the religious imagery shift.
